fixes.explanation: Not the king. Jeroboam is the one who sent her in disguise. Verse 5 says it was the LORD who spoke to Ahijah ahead of time. The news was already waiting before she reached the door.
He does greet her that way. Verse 6 has him say, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam! Why are you disguised?" So the disguise didn't hide who she was from him. I'd ask for a refund on that costume.

Ahijah says it in his own words: "…I have been sent to you with bad news." (1 Kings 14:6). She came hoping for an answer about her boy, and he doesn't dress it up. I think that's a heavy thing to hear at a door.
No peace news here, friend. In verse 6 Ahijah says, "…I have been sent to you with bad news." The rest of the passage shows how heavy it is.

Here God is speaking, and in verse 8 He says David "…kept My commandments and followed Me with all his heart, doing only what was right in My eyes." That's the measure God holds up. It's about David's heart following Him. Heart first, friend, always.

Verse 8 does mention the house of David, as the one the kingdom was torn from. But verse 10 says God will cut off every male belonging to Jeroboam. Nothing there about serving anybody. I think it's a hard sentence.

Ahijah gives the reason in verse 13: "…only in him has the LORD, the God of Israel, found any good in the house of Jeroboam." Out of a whole house, one boy is singled out. I think that's a quiet kindness tucked inside a hard message.
Ahijah says it will. Verse 14 says the LORD "…will raise up for Himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam." The king is raised up for the LORD Himself.

Verse 16 says God will give Israel over "…on account of the sins Jeroboam has committed and has caused Israel to commit." That's two things: what he did and what he led others into. Leaders carry a lot, friend.
